title: orient merges waived findings into the violations array (inflates blocking count)
description:
VERIFIED against code: src/tools/orient.rs:482-486 chains outcome.waived into the violations output — `outcome.active.iter().chain(outcome.waived.iter().map(|w| &w.finding))` — then serializes every entry with severity:blocking and NO waived marker. check::evaluate already partitions active vs waived correctly upstream; orient re-merges them. A reader can't distinguish active from waived without hand-diffing file paths against the waivers array. This is the "violations counted pre-waiver-partition" contract hazard called out in sutra/CLAUDE.md (bitten 3× before).

FIX: either (a) put waived findings in a separate `waived_violations` array, or (b) add `waived: true` + the waiver rationale to each merged entry so active/blocking is not overstated. Orient-local — review/constraints unaffected.

GATED on sutra/312 (delete-or-realign orient): if orient is deleted this closes wontfix; the merge disappears with it.
reproduction: Run sutra_orient on a scope with waived constraint findings (e.g. sutra src/conventions/engine.rs, which has 15 waived no-clone-driven-dev entries). The `violations` array lists ~37 entries all at severity:blocking, most of which are actually waived; the waivers are only in a separate `waivers` array with no back-reference.

messages.text: wontfix — superseded by sutra/312 (delete orient). The waived-into-violations merge disappears with the tool. Kept as verified negative knowledge: real bug at src/tools/orient.rs:482-486, which chained outcome.waived into the violations array with severity:blocking and no waived marker. check::evaluate partitions active/waived correctly upstream; orient re-merged them. Lesson for any future surface: never re-merge active+waived findings without a per-entry waived flag or a separate array — this is the pre-waiver-partition contract hazard that has bitten this repo repeatedly.
